routes.summary: Redeems a sign-in's one-time code, with the verifier of the challenge it was started with, for a session: the same response a password sign-in gives. A sign-up's code creates the Free tenant and its first user first.
Confirms linking an identity to an account, with the link e-mailed to the account's address, and signs the user in.
The identity providers people can sign in with, and whether they can sign up with one.
Where the provider sends the browser back to. Redirects to the portal's `/login/sso` page with a one-time `code`, or with an `error` code, and the sign-in's `intent`.

Starts a sign-in with `provider` (`github`, `google` or `microsoft`): a browser navigation, which redirects to the provider, or to the portal with an `error` code. `intent` is `signin` (the default), `signup` or `link`; `codeChallenge` is the S256 challenge of a verifier the portal keeps for the exchange; `loginHint` optionally suggests an account.
The tenant's low-balance alerts.
Sets the tenant's low-balance alerts.
The tenant's auto top-up: whether it's on, its threshold and amount, and whether it stopped after a failure.
Turns auto top-up on or off. Saving again restarts one that stopped after a failed charge.
The tenant's prepaid balance.
The plans on sale, with what each includes and costs, to compare with the tenant's own.
The tenant's latest billing notices (what its Billing webhooks were sent and its admins emailed), newest first.
The tenant's effective plan: tier, allowances, limits, lanes and prices.
Where the tenant stands: its plan and its state (frozen after a failed renewal, a change on its way), its balance, whether it can start work, and this period's use of each allowance.
The tenant's builds, newest first. Filters: `namespace` (repeatable), `outcome`, `isDeploy`.

queryParams.description: Only builds that ended this way: `Succeeded`, `Failed` or `Rejected` (case-insensitive).

routes.summary: Removes a build's record (and the sources it holds) at once. 404 outside the caller's tenant.
One build, with its manifest, sources, log and what it deployed. 404 outside the caller's tenant.

One command or operation of a capsule run, with its status, exit code and output. A command still queued or running when the run ended reads as `AbortedOnTermination`, so a caller waiting for it always sees an end.

Disables one version of a connector. It is never used again, so every tool version built on it, and every agent, interaction, app and code pipeline pinned to those, fails until the version is re-enabled or they are redeployed onto another one. Safe to repeat; the change is audit-logged.
Re-enables a disabled connector version. Safe to repeat; the change is audit-logged.
The tenant's credential stacks, by name.

Creates a credential stack from the tenant's own credentials, in the order runs try them. Each entry can narrow what its credential serves: only some models, only some endpoint kinds, or switched off.
Deletes a stack. Refused while it's the tenant's or a namespace's default.
A credential stack: its entries, in the order runs try them, and each entry's rules.
Replaces a stack's name, description and entries. Runs already going keep the stack as it was when they started; runs started after use the new one.
Where a credential stack is used: whether it's the tenant's default, the namespaces whose default it is, and the knowledge bases that embed with it. While any of these use it, it can't be deleted.
A credential stack by its name (unique in the tenant), as a start request's `credentialStack` names it.
Deletes every credential with the tag (and takes them out of their stacks); returns how many.
The tenant's credentials, by name; optionally only those with `tag`.
Creates a credential; returns it, with its id.
Deletes a credential, and takes it out of every stack that holds it.
A credential: its provider, models, endpoint, tag and health, and a hint of each key (never the key).
Replaces a credential's fields. Keys are matched by id; an existing key sent without a value keeps its secret.

Replaces the tokens of a credential made with `POST /credentials/sign-in-tokens`, after you refreshed them. Its name, description and tag stay as they are, and it gets a fresh start if it was switched off for failing. A sign-in made through Maitento's own sign-in flow is refused: Maitento refreshes those itself.

Tests the credential: each key lists the provider's models once, which proves the key is accepted without running a model. A test that passes switches a credential its circuit breaker turned off back on. Limited to a few a minute per tenant.

Makes an OAuth credential from a Claude or Codex sign-in whose tokens you already hold, such as one your own application signed in. You keep the tokens fresh: Maitento never refreshes them, and you replace them with `PUT /credentials/by-id/{id}/sign-in-tokens` after each refresh. The tokens are write-only.

Starts signing a coding agent's subscription in as an OAuth credential (`claude` or `codex`), or, with a credential id, signing an existing one in again. Returns where the person finishes it and the sign-in's id.
Finishes a sign-in: Claude's with the code Anthropic showed; Codex's by polling until the person has entered the code (`Pending` until then). Returns the saved credential once it's done.

Tests a credential before saving it, so a failing one never has to exist: the same checks and calls as testing a saved one, on the keys in the body. Nothing is stored. The body is what creating it takes, and is refused with the same codes. Shares the saved test's limit.

Disables one version of a tool. It is never used again, so every agent, interaction, app and code pipeline pinned to it fails until the version is re-enabled or they are redeployed onto another one. Safe to repeat; the change is audit-logged.
Re-enables a disabled tool version. Safe to repeat; the change is audit-logged.
Searches the documents in knowledge bases (partitions) for the passages closest in meaning to a query.
Erasure of the loom and everything woven in it (data-subject erasure, not forgetting).
Asks for the loom to be night-woven now. Accepted, not done: the weaving runs in the background.
The patterns the loom keeps (the shape of each codebase its agents work in), most recently changed first.
Erasure of a codebase's pattern. There is no undo.
The pattern of one codebase, matched as a subject is (case and spacing do not matter).
Shapes the pattern of a codebase, creating it if need be: replaces its architecture (an empty one clears it), adds heuristics, key files and conventions, and drops items by the start of their text.
Inheritance: copies the strongest shared knowledge of another loom of the tenant into this one.
What an agent would wake up knowing if these subjects walked in (repeat `subjects` per subject).
Erasure of one thread (data-subject erasure, not forgetting: agents cut, they do not unravel).
Gives a thread to another loom of the tenant. It arrives second-hand, marked with where it came from; a loom that already holds it has its own thread strengthened instead (`Reinforced`).
Night weavings across every loom of the tenant, changed at or after `since`, oldest change first: what night weaving did and spent. A night's token usage is recorded on the night as it is spent.
The stack runs of this namespace's definitions use when neither their start nor their definition names one.
Sets a namespace's default stack, or clears it with a null id, so its runs fall back to the tenant's.
The namespace's web-tool settings: the temporary partition its runs' web fetches default to.

Validates a project's definitions, or with `isDeploy` deploys them. Any member can validate; deploying needs a tenant admin, because what it deploys (apps above all) runs with the tenant's own rights, and anyone else is refused with 403 `api:builds:deploy-requires-admin`.
One namespace's builds, newest first (same paging and filters; the route names the namespace).

routes.summary: Marks the partition's embedding-key failures as reported, removing it from `GET /partitions/embedding-credential-failures`. The failures stay recorded; this only says the tenant's administrators have been told.

Sets the credential stack the partition embeds with, or clears it with a null `credentialStackId`. While one is set, the partition's own embedding keys are tried first, then the stack's keys, in place of the tenant's model keys and default stack; Maitento's key is never used. Resumes a re-index that stopped for want of keys.
Removes the partition's embedding keys and fallback setting, so it embeds with Maitento's own key again.

Replaces the partition's embedding keys (the tenant's own keys for its embedding provider, in failover order) and whether it may fall back to Maitento's key, clearing any recorded failures. Resumes a failed re-index when the keys or the fallback setting actually changed; sending the same values again does not.

Sets the partition's embedding profile (provider, model, width, chunking) together with the keys and fallback setting for that provider. A profile that changes the index starts a destructive re-index: the partition's vectors are discarded, every document is re-embedded, and search on the partition fails with `api:embeddings:index-rebuilding` until it completes. Such a change is refused while a re-index is running (`api:embeddings:reindex-in-progress`), and refused with nothing changed when the request has `allowReindex: false` (`api:embeddings:reindex-not-permitted`): send that to update keys without ever rebuilding. Sending the current profile again only updates the keys: it is allowed mid-rebuild, and resumes a failed rebuild when the keys or fallback setting changed, or when `allowReindex` is true (a deliberate retry).
The partition's files, newest first, without their extracted text (read `GET /files/by-id/{id}` for that). `cursor` is the previous page's `nextCursor`; `limit` defaults to 50, clamped to 1–200.
The partitions whose embedding keys have failed and need an admin to fix or replace a key. Normally an empty array: check this one list rather than reading every partition.
The embedding models a partition may be indexed with, with their widths and chunking limits. Build a model picker from this rather than keeping your own copy of the list.

A test call: embeds one short text with the given profile and keys and reports the width that came back, or a stable error code when it failed (a failed test is still a 200: the outcome is the answer). Use it to confirm a custom model's width before choosing it; changing a partition to a custom model runs the same test before rebuilding anything. It never uses Maitento's key, stores nothing, and returns no provider response text.
The effective embedding profile and index (re-index progress) state of up to 500 partitions in one call. A PUT because the id list is a body, not because anything is written.
